parts.t: Explore Township of Langley land use plans, OCP maps, and zoning updates to see where future growth, rezoning, and development are happening across Aldergrove, Brookswood-Fernridge, Willoughby, Carvolth, and surrounding communities. These official plans help buyers, sellers, and investors understand changes in density, new housing, and long-term neighbourhood opportunities.

lines.text: The purpose of the Aldergrove Community Plan is to provide for long range orderly development in accordance with stated objectives; guide for day-to-day decision-making in the development process of the area; the basis for the preparation and adoption of the capital works program based on need; and the basis for the preparation and adoption of land use regulating bylaws and amendments to them.

The Brookswood–Fernridge Community Plan forms part of the Township of Langley’s Official Community Plan (OCP), establishing the long-range vision for sustainable neighbourhood growth. Any detailed neighbourhood plans that apply to portions of this area must align with the guiding policies of the Community Plan.

The Carvolth Neighbourhood Plan (Bylaw No. 4995) was repealed by the Township of Langley on June 15, 2026. The Carvolth area, around the Carvolth Transit Exchange at 86 Avenue and 202 Street, is now covered by the Willoughby Transit Corridor Plan (Bylaw No. 6202). That plan sets land use, density and design policies for transit-oriented growth along 200 Street, with a transit hub planned at the exchange.

The Central Gordon Estate Neighbourhood Plan (Bylaw No. 4924) was repealed by the Township of Langley on June 15, 2026. It has been combined with the North East Gordon Estate plan into the Gordon Neighbourhood Plan (Bylaw No. 6203), which now guides land use, housing density, environmental protection, community facilities and servicing for this part of southeast Willoughby.

The Jericho Sub-Neighbourhood Plan (Bylaw No. 4825) was repealed by the Township of Langley on June 15, 2026. The Jericho area is now covered by the Willoughby Transit Corridor Plan (Bylaw No. 6202), which combines five former neighbourhood plans in western Willoughby into one plan. It sets land use, density, park and servicing policies for transit-oriented growth around future transit hubs along 200 Street.

The Latimer Neighbourhood Plan (Bylaw No. 5101) was repealed by the Township of Langley on June 15, 2026. Latimer is now covered by the Willoughby Transit Corridor Plan (Bylaw No. 6202), part of the Willoughby Community Plan. It sets land use, density and servicing policies for the 200 Street corridor, including a planned transit hub at 84 Avenue next to Latimer Village.

Murrayville is located along both sides of the Fraser Highway, just east of Langley City. The area covers roughly 550 hectares (1,360 acres). Primarily residential and agricultural, it also contains pockets of commercial and industrial activity.

The North East Gordon Estate Neighbourhood Plan (Bylaw No. 4475) was repealed by the Township of Langley on June 15, 2026. It has been combined with the Central Gordon Estate plan into the Gordon Neighbourhood Plan (Bylaw No. 6203), which now sets policy for residential and commercial land use, the natural environment, community facilities, and water, sewer and drainage servicing in southeast Willoughby.

The Routley Neighbourhood Plan (Bylaw No. 4013) was repealed by the Township of Langley on June 15, 2026. Routley, the area bounded by 68 Avenue, 196 Street, 200 Street and approximately 73A Avenue, is now covered by the Willoughby Transit Corridor Plan (Bylaw No. 6202). That plan sets land use, density and design policies for transit-oriented growth along 200 Street, including a transit hub at 72 Avenue.

The Smith Neighbourhood Plan provides detailed land-use direction for an area within Willoughby and is supported by an Engineering Services Plan that identifies required and future infrastructure. This includes transportation systems, utilities, stormwater management, and community services to guide development.

Walnut Grove is a major growth area in the Township of Langley. First initiated in 1979, the Walnut Grove Community Plan outlines a self-contained community with a strong residential base and complementary commercial and institutional services.

The Williams Neighbourhood Plan defines the long-term vision, goals, and policies guiding growth over the next 20+ years. It includes frameworks for land use, open space, pedestrian connections, mobility, community identity, infrastructure, and financial planning, helping shape a complete and vibrant neighbourhood.

The Yorkson Neighbourhood Plan provides comprehensive guidance for future growth by establishing a decision-making framework for land use, the natural environment, transportation, engineering services, and community amenities. Its core objective is to maintain a high quality of life for current and future Yorkson residents, based on the principles of completeness, livability, fiscal accountability, economic prosperity, and environmental stewardship.
